extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Official MPEP guidance on conducting, scheduling, recordation, and limits of interviews (personal, telephonic, video, electronic mail) during patent prosecution and on formally making amendments to applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an interview
rubrics_metrics.description: The personal appearance of an applicant, attorney, or agent before the examiner or a telephone conversation or video conference or electronic mail between such parties presenting matters for the examiner’s consideration is considered an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews encompass face-to-face, telephonic, video conference, and electronic mail communications when substantive matters are presented for the examiner’s consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location and hours for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews with examiners ... must be conducted on Office premises and within Office hours, as the respective examiners may designate. Interviews will not be permitted at any other time or place without the authority of the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews are permissible during normal business hours Monday through Friday except examiner overtime hours. Video conferencing via USPTO VCC or PTRC is available as authorized official business during normal business hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may require that an interview be scheduled in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interview should normally be arranged in advance (letter, facsimile, electronic mail, telegram or telephone) to ensure the primary examiner and/or examiner in charge will be present. Examiner may require an Applicant Initiated Interview Request (PTOL-413A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews before first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview for the discussion of the patentability of a pending application will not occur before the first Office action, unless the application is a continuing or substitute application or the examiner determines that such an interview would advance prosecution of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For interviews before the first official action in non-continuing applications, the examiner may require the applicant to provide a paper including state of the art and up to three closest references with explanation of how the broadest claim distinguishes over them (see 37 CFR 1.133(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordation of interview substance
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete written statement as to the substance of any face-to-face, video conference, electronic mail or telephone interview with regard to the merits of an application must be made of record in the application, whether or not an agreement with the examiner was reached at the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.133(b). Examiners must complete Interview Summary form PTOL-413 for each substantive interview (or PTOL-413B if examiner-initiated and will provide summary). The substance of any interview must be placed in the application file; omission may lead to a one-month notice to supply the omission or risk abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant written statement after interview when requesting reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: In every instance where reconsideration is requested in view of an interview with an examiner, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview as warranting favorable action must be filed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interview does not remove the necessity for reply to Office actions as specified in §§ 1.111 and 1.135.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using Internet e-mail like an interview without authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet e-mail shall NOT be used to conduct an exchange or communications similar to those exchanged during telephone or personal interviews unless a written authorization from the applicants or an attorney/agent of record has been given to use Internet e-mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authorized, a paper copy of the Internet e-mail contents MUST be made and placed in the patent application file as required by the Federal Records Act in the same manner as an Examiner Interview Summary Form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Video Conference Center (VCC) and PTRCs
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO VCC is available for authorized official business during normal business hours; PTRCs may provide video-conferencing but not all PTRCs have capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customers should contact the desired PTRC to ensure availability and identify two alternative dates/times. An interview in the Video Conference Center must be arranged at least 3 days in advance. The examiner coordinates scheduling through the PTRC Program office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Initiated Interview Request form (PTOL-413A) recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant is initiating a request for an interview, an 'Applicant Initiated Interview Request' form (PTOL-413A) should be submitted to the examiner prior to the interview ... This form should identify the participants, proposed date, whether personal/telephonic/video, and include a brief description of the issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will accept PTOL-413A as indication the practitioner is authorized to conduct the interview. A copy of the completed PTOL-413A should be attached to PTOL-413 at completion. Failure to submit PTOL-413A is not by itself grounds to deny the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation requirement for interview participants
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview should be had only when the nature of the case is such that the interview could serve to develop and clarify specific issues ... the attorney when presenting himself or herself for an interview should be fully prepared to discuss the issues raised in the Office action. When it is obvious that the attorney is not so prepared, an interview should not be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is desirable that the attorney indicate in advance what issues to discuss by submitting, in writing, a proposed amendment to permit examiner preparation and focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner conduct during interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should avoid unnecessary interruptions during interviews ... should not take incoming telephone calls unless such are of an emergency nature. Examiners should familiarize themselves with the status and existing issues in an application before an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may state claims require further search/study and may conclude interview if no common ground; should attempt to identify issues and resolve differences during the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the responsibility of both parties to the interview to see that it is not extended beyond a reasonable period, usually not longer than 30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primary examiner must ensure the interview is not extended beyond a reasonable period even when not personally participating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews with pro se applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: During an interview with an applicant who is prosecuting his or her own case and is not familiar with Office procedure the examiner may make suggestions that will advance the prosecution of this case; this lies wholly within his or her discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too much time should not be allowed for such interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling agreements reached at interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Where agreement is reached as a result of an interview, applicant’s representative should be advised that an amendment pursuant to the agreement should be promptly submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment prepares the case for final action, the examiner should take the case up as special; otherwise await its turn. Consideration of a filed amendment may be had by hand delivery of a duplicate copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTOL-413 Interview Summary contents and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must complete an Interview Summary form PTOL-413 for each interview where a matter of substance has been discussed ... The PTOL-413 form provides for recordation of: (A) application number; (B) name of applicant; (C) name of examiner; (D) date of interview; (E) type of interview; (F) participants; (G) whether an exhibit was shown; (H) claims discussed; (I) specific prior art discussed; (J) whether an agreement was reached and description; (K) signature of examiner; (L) names of other USPTO personnel present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTOL-413 should be given a paper number, placed in right-hand portion of file, listed on Contents list; duplicate copy given to applicant in personal interviews or mailed/faxed for telephonic/video/email interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum items for complete interview record
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete and proper recordation ... should include at least the following applicable items: (A) brief description of any exhibit shown; (B) identification of the claims discussed; (C) identification of specific prior art discussed; (D) identification of principal proposed amendments of a substantive nature discussed; (E) the general thrust of the principal arguments of the applicant and the examiner; (F) general indication of any other pertinent matters discussed; (G) if appropriate, the general results or outcome of the interview; (H) in electronic mail case, a paper copy of the e-mail contents placed in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of arguments need not be lengthy—general nature or thrust sufficient. Interview Summary alone is not complete unless supplemented to include these items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review and correction of applicant interview summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are expected to carefully review the applicant’s record of the substance of an interview. If the record is not complete or accurate, the examiner may give the applicant a 1-month time period to complete the reply under 37 CFR 1.135(c) where the record is in a reply to a nonfinal Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an inaccuracy bears directly on patentability, the examiner should point it out in the next Office letter or send a letter setting forth the examiner's version. If accurate, examiner should mark 'Interview record OK' with date and initials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, one interview after final rejection is permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to the interview the intended purpose and content should be presented briefly in writing. Such an interview may be granted if examiner is convinced disposal or clarification for appeal may be accomplished with only nominal further consideration. Interviews merely to restate arguments or to discuss new limitations requiring more than nominal reconsideration or new search should be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews prohibited or limited in special situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in unusual situations, no interview is permitted after the brief on appeal is filed or after an application has been passed to issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for interviews after notice of allowance or when application sent to issue require special approval. Office employees forbidden to hold communications with unregistered/suspended attorneys except when they are applicant. Interviews are generally not granted to persons lacking authority to bind applicant; mere power to inspect is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority required to conduct interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are generally not granted to registered individuals who are known to be the local representatives of the attorney in the application unless a power of attorney or Authorization to Act in a Representative Capacity is of record ... The Office will accept PTOL-413A as indication practitioner authorized to conduct interview on behalf of the principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to 37 CFR 10.57(c) a practitioner cannot authorize other registered practitioners to conduct interviews without client consent after full disclosure; nonpractitioners cannot be authorized (37 CFR 10.47). For telephone interviews, a facsimile transmission of a power of attorney is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: No ex parte discussion of inter partes questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may not discuss inter partes questions ex parte with any of the interested parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain separation of ex parte prosecution from inter partes matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure of other cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to an interview in the examiner’s room, the examiner should arrange his or her desk so that all files, drawings and other papers, except those necessary in the interview, are placed out of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect confidentiality of other applications and materials during interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrations, exhibits, and models
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention may be exhibited or demonstrated during the interview by a model or exhibit. A model or exhibit will not generally be admitted as part of the record of an application. A model or exhibit submitted by the applicant which complies with 37 CFR 1.91 would be made part of the application record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the model/exhibit is merely for demonstration it will not be part of the record; a full description of what was demonstrated must be made of record. Demonstrations too large to bring into the Office may be viewed outside the Office with supervisory approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video tape viewing during interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorneys or applicants wishing to show a video tape during an examiner interview must be able to demonstrate that the content has a bearing on an outstanding issue and its viewing will advance prosecution. Prior approval must be granted by the supervisory patent examiner; use of the room and equipment must be granted by the Office of Patent Training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be made at least 1 week in advance. Video equipment in Office of Patent Training only; scheduling must be done through the examiner, not by applicant contacting Office of Patent Training directly. Substance of interview including summary of video must be made of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouped interviews for remote practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: For attorneys remote from the Washington, D.C. area who prefer personal or video conference interviews, the grouped interview practice is effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a prearranged interview includes agreement to file a prompt supplemental amendment putting the case in condition for concluding action, prompt filing gives the application special status and brings it up for immediate special action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must comply with rules and show changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in applications ... are made by filing a paper, in compliance with § 1.52, directing that specified amendments be made. Amendments to the specification must be made by adding, deleting or replacing a paragraph ... replacement paragraphs must show markings to show all changes relative to previous version: added text by underlining; deleted matter by strike-through or double brackets for small deletions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full text of replacement paragraphs and instructions to identify location must be provided; text of any added paragraphs without underlining; deleted paragraph text must not be presented with strike-through when deleting—use instruction to delete identified by paragraph number or text snippet.
